## QUESTION 1

__Write an SQL query that provides playerID, yearID, and batting average for players with at least 1 at bat that year. Sort the table from highest batting average to lowest, and then by playerid alphabetically. Show the top 5 results in your report.__

The table shows the top three players, along with the year that they played and their batting average that year. Each player was at bat at least 1 time and the top 5 all had 100% batting average for that year. The other top 5 players are also listed in the table below.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
import sqlite3
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

sqlite_file = 'lahmansbaseballdb.sqlite'

con = sqlite3.connect(sqlite_file)

# The code below can serve as a template for all the rest of your queries. It is just missing the
# SQL code. Put your SQL query in between the triple quotation marks to create the query. The records will be stored in 'results', which is a polars data frame

q = """
  SELECT playerID, 
         yearID, 
         (CAST(H AS REAL) / AB) * 100 AS `BA`
  FROM battingpost
  WHERE AB >= 1
  ORDER BY BA DESC
  LIMIT 5;
    """
results = pl.read_database(q, con)
results

```

## QUESTION 3

__Now modify the SQL query to calculate the batting average for players over their entire careers (all years combined). Only include players with at least 100 at bats over their entire career, and print the top 5 results.__

The person with the highest batting average over their entire career was molitpa01 with a batting average of 36.75%. The rest of the top 5 are also listed in the table.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
import sqlite3
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

sqlite_file = 'lahmansbaseballdb.sqlite'

con = sqlite3.connect(sqlite_file)

# The code below can serve as a template for all the rest of your queries. It is just missing the
# SQL code. Put your SQL query in between the triple quotation marks to create the query. The records will be stored in 'results', which is a polars data frame

q = """
  SELECT playerID,
         (CAST(SUM(H) AS REAL) / SUM(AB)) * 100 AS BA
  FROM battingpost
  GROUP BY playerID\
  HAVING SUM(AB) >= 100
  ORDER BY BA DESC
  LIMIT 5;
    """
results = pl.read_database(q, con)
results
```
